photo.caption: Green electroluminescence from a point contact on a crystal of SiC recreates Round's original experiment from 1907.
photo.description: This image shows a replication of H.J. Round's experiments in which he discovered the effect underlying the light emitting diode (LED). A negatively charged needle contacts a positively charged crystal of silicon carbide or carborundum. At a voltage of 9 V and a current of 30 mA a green glow can be observed at the contact point between needle and crystal. A more detailed version of the setup can be found at www.dlip.de
